title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 95-97): Grothendieck is setting up a combinatorics of graphs to describe the stratification 'at infinity' of M_{g,ν}. These are dual graphs of degenerate (stable) curves with ν marked points.

On the previous page he encodes a finite topological 1-complex X with a finite vertex set S as a system (S, Â, σ, o). Here Â is a finite set of half-edges, σ is an involution of Â, and o: Â → S is the 'origin' map. When σ has no fixed points this is an ordinary graph: Serre-style, with loops and multiple edges allowed.

This page drops the fixed-point-free condition.
- The fixed-point set I = Â^σ consists of 'bandes aplaties' (flattened bands).
- Topologically these are the boundary points of X ('pts-bord') that are not in S, i.e. half-open edges ending freely.
- Writing Â = I ⊔ Ã with Ã = Â \ I, the data is equivalent to an ordinary graph (S, Ã, σ_Ã, o_Ã) plus a finite set I and a map I → S.

In modern language this is a graph with legs (tails), and the free ends play the role of marked points. It is exactly the 'flags with an involution whose fixed points are legs' formalism later used for stable graphs of M̄_{g,n} and for modular operads.

Drawing conventions:
- Vertices are drawn as fat dots.
- Legs are drawn as free segments without a dot.
- The example has five vertices: a double edge, a loop, and five free legs.
- A second sketch, 'with the notation of numbered points', labels the legs 1, 2, 3 (it seems to show a different or partial example).

Purpose: the next page uses this to describe how a deeper boundary stratum G' arises from G. One chooses a set C of ordinary edges and cuts each edge at an interior point, which creates new pairs of legs. The result is again a graph with legs, possibly disconnected. One then discards some legs and selects connected components. This is the cutting/gluing (clutching) combinatorics of boundary strata, i.e. of modular operads.
errors: No mathematical error. There is a notational slip: 'en désignant Î ou I ⊔ Ã' should read 'Â (= Î) = I ⊔ Ã'. Â and Î are used interchangeably for the full set of half-edges.

Minor: the topological description on the previous page (components of X∖S non-compact, S→π0(X) surjective) needs to be adjusted to allow free boundary ends. This page does that implicitly by calling legs boundary points of X not in S, but does not restate the conditions.

ideas.what: Graph as (vertices S, half-edges Â, involution σ, origin map o: Â→S), with fixed points of σ interpreted as free legs ('bandes aplaties')
ideas.modern_name: Graph with legs/tails in the flag formalism (flags F, involution ι, ∂: F→V; legs = ι-fixed flags)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kontsevich–Manin (1994), Getzler–Kapranov (modular operads, 1998), Behrend–Manin. The fixed-point-free version goes back to Serre, 'Arbres, amalgames, SL2' (1977).
ideas.where_published: Not as such. Esquisse d'un programme discusses the Teichmüller tower and dual graphs of stable curves only informally.

ideas.what: Topological model: legs = boundary points of a compact 1-complex X not belonging to the vertex set S
ideas.modern_name: Geometric realization of a graph with half-open legs

ideas.what: Legs labelled by marked points ('points numérotés') as the dual-graph encoding of ν-pointed degenerate curves
ideas.modern_name: Stable (dual) graph of a pointed nodal curve, legs labelled 1..n
ideas.usually_credited_to: Knudsen / Deligne–Mumford era; systematized by Kontsevich–Manin

missed.claim: This is an early (likely early 1980s) independent appearance of the half-edge-with-involution-fixed-points-as-legs formalism. It is applied to the boundary structure of M_{g,ν}, and the following page describes cutting edges into pairs of legs. That predates the standard Kontsevich–Manin/Getzler–Kapranov formalization by about a decade. The idea itself is natural and now standard, so this matters historically rather than mathematically.
missed.quote: On n'exige plus que σ soit sans pts fixes — l'ens des pts fixes, I, correspond aux "bandes aplaties"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority and context for the modular-operad and stable-graph formalism within Grothendieck's Teichmüller-tower programme. It is not a new mathematical result.

deep.surprise_reason: Clean, correct but routine combinatorial definition: graphs with legs via an involution with fixed points. It is now textbook material. The only interest is that it is an early, independent appearance in Grothendieck's M_{g,ν} notes.
transcription_corrections: 'en désignant Î ou I ⊔ Ã' — read as 'désignant Î ... = I ⊔ Ã'. The hat/tilde notation (Â, Î) is inconsistent in both the manuscript and the transcription.
In the line 'des 1-complexes i.e. aux [...] "pts-bord"', the struck word before "pts-bord" is unreadable (possibly 'Bords').

Description of the first figure: one vertex carries two free legs (top), the central vertex has one upward free leg, a double edge joins it to a middle vertex, then a single edge leads to a vertex with a loop, and a lower vertex carries two free legs.
